name: The Telescopes
label: Creation
lede: Stephen Lawrie started the Telescopes in Burton upon Trent as a feedback machine, turned it into something gentler on Creation, and has kept the name going under shifting line-ups ever since.

eras.title: Beyond the realm of natural vision
eras.text: Stephen Lawrie grew up between Northumberland, the Midlands and Holland, and came back to the Midlands at 16 to start bands. The one that stuck formed in Burton upon Trent, a brewery town, and went through four or five line-ups before it cut a note.

years.src: It's Psychedelic, Baby! · NME · Wikipedia: The Telescopes
years.h: Lawrie names his band after a telescope's job description
years.p: The line-up that records: Lawrie, David Fitzgerald on lead guitar, Jo Doran on guitar and vocals, Robert Brooks on bass and Dominic Dillon on drums.
years.xp:
Lawrie took the name from a definition: a telescope is "beyond the realm of natural vision." He wanted music with enough layers that it took several listens to see all of it.

By then his listening had moved from Bowie and Neil Young to [[The Velvet Underground|94b0fb9d-a066-4823-b2ec-af1d324bcfcf]], Suicide, [[The Stooges|794c6bf2-3241-416f-9b8f-24e2d84a1c4b]] and The 13th Floor Elevators.

years.src: It's Psychedelic, Baby! · Wikipedia: The Telescopes
years.h: First song out is on a flexi shared with Loop
years.p: 'Forever Close Your Eyes' backs a Loop track on a Cheree flexi given away with the Sowing Seeds fanzine. It was cut down to fit the space left on the disc.
years.xp: Lawrie recorded it on his friend Jake's four-track. The full song ran longer than a flexi could hold, so the band trimmed it.

eras.title: Kick the wall, then the perfect needle
eras.text: Two singles on Cheree and an album on What Goes On, all noise and feedback. Producer Richard Formby helped Lawrie treat the studio as an instrument.

years.cap: Stephen Lawrie at the Jericho Tavern, Oxford, 1989
years.h: A Lincoln show lands them on Cheree with 'Kick the Wall'
years.p: Mike Stout approaches the band after a gig at the In-Psychclopedia in Lincoln and puts them with Leeds producer Richard Formby. AllMusic heard [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]] in the debut single.

yt: 'The Perfect Needle' live at the Falcon, Camden, 1989
years.h: 'The Perfect Needle' becomes the song people know them by
years.p: The What Goes On single climbs to No. 5 on the indie chart and becomes the song people know them by. Cheree's '7th# Disaster' came earlier the same year.

q: Music became as much like painting as performing.
years.src: It's Psychedelic, Baby! · Wikipedia: Taste · Isolation Records
years.h: Taste: bass drones through a desk fan
years.p: Recorded in June 1989 with Formby producing, for What Goes On. Tape loops, a bass drone run through a fan, and on 'Oil Seed Rape' an amp head thrown on the floor with the spring reverb up full.
years.xp:
"Music became as much like painting as performing for me during those sessions," Lawrie said in 2019.

Julian Overton added violin. NME gave it 7/10, and Stuart Maconie wrote that whatever speed you played it at, "it always sounded like the wrong speed." In 2016 Pitchfork put it at No. 47 on its list of the 50 best shoegaze albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Taste · AllMusic · Wikipedia: The Telescopes
years.h: What Goes On folds; Cheree puts Taste back out
years.p: The label goes bankrupt within a year of the album. Cheree reissues Taste, and Fierce releases the live set Trade Mark of Quality.

eras.title: Creation, and the noise turns elegant
eras.text: Alan McGee's Creation Records was home to My Bloody Valentine, Ride and Slowdive when the Telescopes arrived. The singles on the way to their second album pulled the feedback back and let melody through.

years.src: AllMusic · Wikipedia: The Telescopes · Stereo Embers
years.h: Creation picks them up; 'Flying' scrapes the singles chart
years.p: After What Goes On's collapse the band moves to [[Alan McGee|ffacc13a-01e5-4b5d-a455-6a7f302ac9ce]]'s label. 'Celeste' and 'Flying' follow, and 'Flying' reaches the lower end of the UK Singles Chart.
years.xp: McGee managed the band for a while too. "Total conflict of interest," Lawrie said in 2015.

q: Your idea of perfection changes as you move on.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Telescopes (album) · Wikipedia: The Telescopes · AllMusic · Isolation Records
years.h: Guy Fixsen produces the second album, the softer one
years.p: Eleven Lawrie songs, opening with 'Splashdown'. Fans also call it High'r 'n' High'r after the words on the sleeve.
years.xp:
Alexis Petridis heard "an almost fragile sense of elegance and melody" in the new sound. Lawrie said the band still tried "just as many mad ideas"; they just worked "to a different end."

The sound moved toward sixties psychedelia, with sitar, cello and piano. Lawrie remembers McGee falling ill and stepping back from the label soon after the sessions, which left the band in limbo.

AllMusic calls the record a landmark of the shoegaze era. Rev-Ola reissued it in 2004 as #Untitled Second, with two extra tracks.

years.h: The original line-up splits over creative differences
years.p: NME and AllMusic both date the end of the first Telescopes to 1994.

eras.title: Unisex, Antenna, and a third wave
eras.text: Lawrie spent the mid-1990s learning to record on computers so he could work without a studio budget, and started a label for other people's bands. The Telescopes name came back in 2002.

years.h: Lawrie and Doran regroup as Unisex
years.p: The two work together again under a new name. Lawrie also starts Antenna Records to put out other bands' records.

years.src: It's Psychedelic, Baby! · Wikipedia: The Telescopes
years.h: The name returns with cello, violin and vibraphone
years.p: Third Wave comes out on Double Agent. Lawrie found the string and vibes players through the Musicians' Union.

years.src: It's Psychedelic, Baby! · Wikipedia: The Telescopes
years.h: #4 sounds electronic. Much of it is guitar
years.p: Released on Lawrie's Antenna label, built with an EDP Wasp synth, theremins and guitars played in odd ways.
years.xp: "A lot of the sounds on #4 are actually guitars btw. They're just not played in the traditional way," Lawrie said in 2019. Meeting Randall Nieman of [[Füxa|0c291615-ff4a-4c55-9404-2a829484c2cc]], whose gear reminded him of the early Telescopes, pushed him that way.

years.h: Jo Doran leaves after two decades beside Lawrie
years.p: From here the Telescopes are Lawrie plus whoever he's working with, anywhere from solo to about 20 players.

eras.title: Portishead calls, the tapes keep rolling
eras.text: A new generation of psych and drone bands came looking for the Telescopes, and Lawrie toured the US with some of them. The records came faster than ever, most of them on Germany's Tapete.

years.cap: The Telescopes live at Nambucca, London
years.h: [[Portishead|8f6bd1e4-fbe1-4f50-aa9b-94c450ec0f11]] book them for their ATP weekender
years.p: At the I'll Be Your Mirror festival at Alexandra Palace in London, curated by Portishead, the band plays songs from Taste.

years.h: HARM is recorded live on the West Coast
years.p: Cut during a 2013 US tour with members of LSD and the Search for God and Ricky Maymi of The Brian Jonestown Massacre, released on Neon Sigh as two long drone tracks.

years.src: It's Psychedelic, Baby! · Wikipedia: The Telescopes · The Quietus
years.p: Made mostly live with other musicians. The same year brings the Creation box Splashdown and a 17-track tribute album, Anticipating Nowhere.
years.xp: The Quietus's Jeremy Allen: "few groups manage to conflate sensory overload with such a keen sense of melody." The closing track runs 15 minutes.

years.src: It's Psychedelic, Baby! · Wikipedia: The Telescopes
years.p: Self-recorded and stacked up by Lawrie by himself. Dagger's reviewer called it the Raquel Welch of the year.

years.h: Original noise guitarist David Fitzgerald dies of cancer
years.p: Lawrie called him "a true original, in a field of his own."
years.xp: NME reported the death on December 17. Lawrie's statement called Fitzgerald "the first noise guitarist with The Telescopes and a main protagonist of its cause from the very beginning."

years.cap: Stephen Lawrie, press photo for Experimental Health
years.h: Two albums in one year: Of Tomorrow and Experimental Health
years.p: One on Tapete, one on Weisskalt. In 2024 Fuzz Club issues Growing Eyes Become String, made with One Unique Signal.
